description: Experiment 2: can Sarvam-105B attribute a student's error to the correct knowledge-graph node? Student work is written the way OCR output would look (loose LaTeX, line breaks, no cleanup), so the test is faithful to runtime input.

fields.item_node: the node the PROBLEM is tagged to, i.e. the surface topic. This is what a naive system would blame.
fields.true_node: the node actually responsible for the error. Ground truth.
fields.acceptable_nodes: other node ids a fair grader would accept.
fields.blame_type: prereq = true cause sits below the surface topic (the model must look past the topic). topic = surface topic really is the cause (the model must NOT over-shift). control = no error.

cases.misconception: negative sign applied to only the first term of the bracket
cases.note: The headline case. Quotient rule is applied perfectly; the failure is pure algebra.

cases.misconception: outer derivative taken without multiplying by the derivative of the inner function
cases.note: Must NOT be blamed on trig derivatives. The sine derivative is correct.

cases.student_work:
f'(x) = (d/dx x^2)(d/dx sin x)
= 2x * cos x
= 2x cos x
cases.misconception: believes the derivative of a product is the product of the derivatives
cases.note: Both component derivatives are individually correct.

cases.misconception: arithmetic on negative exponents: computed -3 - 1 as -2
cases.note: Genuinely ambiguous. The power rule was stated correctly and then the arithmetic failed. Both answers accepted.

cases.problem: Find the slope of the tangent to y = sin(x) at x = pi/3.
cases.student_work:
dy/dx = cos(x)
at x = pi/3:  cos(pi/3) = sqrt(3)/2
slope = sqrt(3)/2
cases.misconception: swapped the values of sin and cos at pi/3
cases.note: Calculus is flawless. The student does not know the unit circle.

cases.student_work:
plug in x = 2:
(4 - 4)/(2 - 2) = 0/0
undefined, so the limit does not exist
cases.misconception: treats the indeterminate form 0/0 as proof the limit does not exist
cases.note: Should NOT be blamed on factoring; the student never attempted to factor.

cases.misconception: numerator terms of the quotient rule written in the wrong order
cases.note: The algebra after the misstated rule is actually correct. Must not be blamed on sign distribution.

cases.problem: Find the partial derivative with respect to x of f(x, y) = x^2 y^3.
cases.misconception: differentiated both variables instead of holding y constant
cases.note: Looks like a product rule error but is not. Product rule was applied correctly, to the wrong thing.

cases.problem: The loss is L(w) = w^2. Starting from w = 3 with learning rate 0.1, write the gradient descent update and compute the new w.
cases.misconception: moved along the gradient instead of against it, performing ascent instead of descent
cases.note: The derivative is correct. The concept of descent is not.

cases.problem: Use the limit definition of the derivative to find f'(x) for f(x) = 1/x.
cases.note: The difference quotient was set up correctly. The student cannot subtract fractions.
Fully correct. Tests false positives: the model must not invent an error.

Correct and algebraically equivalent, just left unsimplified. Tests whether the model fabricates a mistake when the form differs from the expected answer. This failure mode would be very damaging in production.
